items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with no imaginary simple roots as in [[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], let $k$ be a field, and let $R= igoplus_{ eta\in Q_+}R( eta)$ be the KLR algebra of a KLR datum on it ([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]). Fix a dominant integral weight $\Lambda\in P^+$ with $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambdaangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]) and choose for every $i\in I$ a monic polynomial $a^\Lambda_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_i$; the standard cyclotomic choice, used when no other data are specified, is $a^\Lambda_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge0$, $
u\in I^n$ and $1\le k\le n$ put
$$a^\Lambda(x_k):=\sum_{
u\in I^n}a^\Lambda_{
u_k}(x_k)e(
u)\in R(n),$$
where $a^\Lambda_i$ is the polynomial of the colour $i$; each $a^\Lambda(x_k)e(
u)$ is homogeneous of degree $2(\alpha_{
u_k}\mid\Lambda)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]] ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **cyclotomic ideal** $J^\Lambda$ is the two-sided ideal of $R$ generated by the elements $a^\Lambda(x_1)e(
u)$, $
u\in I^n$, $n\ge0$; it equals $Ra^\Lambda(x_1)R$ because $a^\Lambda(x_1)=\sum_
u a^\Lambda(x_1)e(
u)$ and $x_1$ commutes with all idempotents, and it is homogeneous. The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is
$$R^\Lambda:= igoplus_{ eta\in Q_+}R^\Lambda( eta),\qquad R^\Lambda( eta):=R( eta) ig/R( eta)a^\Lambda(x_1)R( eta),$$
with the convention $R^\Lambda(0):=k$. The quotient is $\mathbb Z$-graded, $R^\Lambda( eta)=e( eta)R^\Lambda e( eta)$ for $e( eta)=\sum_{
u\in I^ eta}e(
u)$, and $R^\Lambda$ is the direct sum of the local unital pieces $R^\Lambda( eta)$.
**Convention (first strand).** The cyclotomic relation is imposed on the leftmost dot $x_1$, and the induction and restriction functors built on this quotient append and remove strands on the right; the equivalent last-strand formulation is obtained by the word mirror recorded on this page. This side convention is binding for every item below, and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Cyclotomic induction and restriction functors
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] with its first-strand convention, and let $R^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\beta R^\Lambda(\beta)$ be the same non-unital direct sum as for the generic KLR algebra of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $\beta\in Q_+$ and $i\in I$ put $e(\beta,i):=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu\ast i)\in R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$, where $\nu\ast i$ is the word $\nu$ followed by $i$; this is an idempotent. Right-appending the letter $i$ defines a unital graded algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:R^\Lambda(\beta)\longrightarrow R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e(\nu)\mapsto e(\nu\ast i),\quad x_a\mapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\mapsto\tau_a,$$
which is well defined because the relations (1)-(7) only involve the first $|\beta|$ strands and because $\iota_i$ fixes the first-strand cyclotomic generator $a^\Lambda(x_1)$, so it descends to the quotients. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors
$$F^\Lambda_i:\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))\to\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)),\quad F^\Lambda_i(M):=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M,$$
$$E^\Lambda_i:\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i))\to\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),\quad E^\Lambda_i(N):=e(\beta,i)N,$$
where the $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module structures on the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ and on $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ are induced by $\iota_i$, and $\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}$ is the graded balanced tensor product of [[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] in the total-degree grading. Both functors are additive, preserve homogeneous degrees, and commute with internal shifts: $F^\Lambda_i(M\{r\})\cong F^\Lambda_i(M)\{r\}$ and $E^\Lambda_i(N\{r\})\cong E^\Lambda_i(N)\{r\}$ ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). $F^\Lambda_i$ is left adjoint to $E^\Lambda_i$ (Frobenius reciprocity), via the natural degree-zero isomorphisms
$$\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)}(F^\Lambda_i M,N)\cong\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}(M,\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)}(R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i),N))\cong\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}(M,E^\Lambda_i N).$$
As weight-shifting endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda)=\bigoplus_\beta\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$, the composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ are endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$. Exactness, preservation of finitely generated graded projectives, and the exact sequence comparing $F^\Lambda_i$ with the left-append induction are proved below on this page; the same-order right adjunction of the two-category formulation is not asserted here in unshifted form, and the normalized Grothendieck operators used downstream are those recorded in the integrable-action theorem below. This definition is choice-free.
items.strategy: Well-definedness of $\iota_i$: the generic KLR presentation acts on $I^{n}$, and the right-append map sends $e(\nu)$ to $e(\nu\ast i)$; each relation (1)-(7) of the presentation is either position-wise (relations (1),(2),(5)), transported along the same adjacent transpositions (relations (3),(4),(6),(7)), or a far-commutation, so the map extends to $R(n)\to R(n+1)$; it is the partial unit of the block embedding of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] composed with the identification $R(\beta)\cong R(|\beta|)e(\beta)$. On the cyclotomic quotient, $a^\Lambda(x_1)$ is a sum of monomials in $x_1$, unaffected by the right append, so the generator of the ideal maps to the generator of the ideal and $\iota_i$ descends. The bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ inherits the graded $(R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),R^\Lambda(\beta))$-bimodule structure from left multiplication and from $\iota_i$ on the right; $e(\beta,i)$ is a sum of orthogonal idempotents, hence idempotent. The functors are the cyclotomic instances of the generic ones, so additivity and shift compatibility are inherited from HA-18's balanced tensor and internal shift ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]], [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Adjunction: the tensor-Hom adjunction for the bimodule is degree-zero; the middle term identifies $\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)}(R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i),N)$ with $e(\beta,i)N$ by evaluation at $e(\beta,i)$, and the right $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-action corresponds to $\iota_i$. The weight bookkeeping is explicit: $F^\Lambda_i$ raises the weight by $\alpha_i$ and $E^\Lambda_i$ lowers it by $\alpha_i$, so both composites in the statement are endofunctors of the single category $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$; this is the convention in which the two weight-sign cases of the categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation are stated. The right adjunction in the sources (Webster Theorem 1.8, biadjointness up to grading shift) is realized in the two-category normalization with intrinsic bubble shifts and is not an unshifted graded adjunction of these naive functors; the identity of the two normalizations is recorded in the batch notes, and no item of this page uses the second adjunction. No AC is used.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR algebras are finite-dimensional and graded symmetric
items.strategy:
Follow Kang--Kashiwara Section 4.1 and Lauda--Vazirani Proposition 2.3 for (a). Nilpotence: by induction on the position, using that for distinct adjacent colours $
u_a
e
u_{a+1}$ the relation $Q_{
u_a
u_{a+1}}(x_a,x_{a+1})=	au_a^2$ and Lemma 4.2 (the divided-difference identity $(x_{a}-x_{a+1})\partial_a f=s_af-f$ gives $(f-s_af)	au e(
u)=(\partial_af)	au^2e(
u)$ up to the native sign) propagate a monic annihilating polynomial from $x_a$ to $x_{a+1}$, and for equal adjacent colours Kang--Kashiwara Lemma 4.2 directly propagates it through the divided difference; the base case is the defining cyclotomic relation on $x_1$. Finite generation is then immediate from the spanning set $\{	au_w x^ae(
u)\}$ of the PBW theorem [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], finitely many for each $a$-multi-index modulo the monic relations; a finitely generated graded module over a field with bounded-below grading is finite-dimensional, and the PBW spanning set with the monic relations shows that each graded piece is finite-dimensional. Vanishing of $R^\Lambda( eta+k\alpha_i)$ for large $k$ is Kang--Kashiwara Lemma 4.3(b): a monic $g$ with $g(x_n)=0$ and the repeated divided-difference identity $(\partial_{n+m-1}\cdots\partial_n g)(x_n)=\pm1$ force $e(
u)R^\Lambda(n+m)=0$ once the word has $m$ trailing $i$'s, and the induction on $n$ removes the trailing condition. For (b): the closing functional of Webster Section 1.3 is defined on a diagram by capping the right boundary, it is homogeneous of the degree of the cap in the fixed normalization, and it kills no nonzero left ideal because a nonzero left ideal contains an element with nonzero closing scalar (a diagram with a left boundary and a nonzero right-closing survives, and no relation identifies all closings with zero); the proof of Webster Theorem 1.8 derives the Frobenius property from the biadjunction and the uniqueness of the adjoint, and Remark 1.9 adjusts the trace by the crossing scalars $t(i)$ so that the resulting form is cyclic. Evenness of the degree is verified on the rank-one corner, where $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(a^\Lambda_i(x_1))$, the Frobenius form is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_i-1}$ (a triangular pairing on the monomial basis with diagonal units), of degree $2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. For (c): the bimodule isomorphism $R^\Lambda( eta)\cong (R^\Lambda( eta))^\vee\{t^\Lambda( eta)\}$ given by the trace (Frobenius) implies $P^\#\cong P\{t^\Lambda( eta)\}$ for principal projectives, and both sides being additive and commuting with summands, for all finitely generated graded projectives; the duality is an equivalence on finite-dimensional modules because $(-)^\#$ is exact and $(-)^{\#\#}\cong\mathrm{id}$ (evaluation), it reverses shifts by construction, and it exchanges projectives and injectives, which coincide over a Frobenius algebra; indecomposables go to indecomposables because the duality is an equivalence. The parity statement is the specialization of evenness of $t^\Lambda( eta)$; in the standard normalization the closing degree is even because every dot contributes $2d_i$ and the cap contributes an even multiple of the Cartan pairing. No choice principle is used; local finiteness of the algebra is not needed.

items.title: Diagram duality and graded module duals for the cyclotomic quotient
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] over a field $k$, with the finite-dimensional graded symmetric structure of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]. Let $\psi$ be the anti-involution of the KLR presentation that fixes the native generators $x_a,\tau_a,e(\nu)$ (this is the normalization of the source's perfect pairing; the horizontal-reflection mirror of the KLR Cartan pairing [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] is related to it by the word mirror of this page, and the two conventions are recorded at authoring). It descends to $R^\Lambda$ because it fixes the first-strand generator $a^\Lambda(x_1)$. For a finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module $M$ define the **graded dual** $M^\vee:=\mathrm{HOM}_k(M,k)$ with $(r\cdot f)(m):=f(\psi(r)m)$ and the shift convention of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]; write
$$M^\#:=M^\vee,\qquad (M\{r\})^\#\cong M^\#\{-r\},\qquad (M^\#)^\#\cong M$$
via evaluation. **Self-dual normalization.** For an indecomposable finite-dimensional graded module $M$ the dual $M^\#$ is again indecomposable and lies in the shift orbit of $M$; since $(M\{s\})^\#\cong M^\#\{-s\}$, the equation $M\{s\}^\#\cong M\{s\}$ has the unique solution $s=s(M)$ whenever the duality shift $t(M)$ with $M^\#\cong M\{t(M)\}$ is even. This holds for every indecomposable by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]], and the representative $M\{s(M)\}$ is called the **self-dual normalization**; all simples and indecomposable projectives on this page are labelled by their self-dual normalized representatives, and $P^\#$ for a finitely generated graded projective is computed with the same shift bookkeeping ([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]). The normalization is compatible with the generic convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] under the quotient, and with the $\psi$-twisted Cartan pairing; it is fixed once and for all, and any statement transporting a duality uses exactly this shift.
items.strategy: Record the conventions and their well-definedness. $\psi$ fixes the generators $x_a,\tau_a,e(\nu)$; it preserves the cyclotomic ideal because $x_1$ is fixed and the ideal is generated by $x_1$-monomials, hence descends to the quotient. The horizontal-reflection mirror of the generic KLR pairing is its composition with the word mirror $\rho$; both are anti-involutions, $\rho\psi=\psi\rho$, and the relation between the two pairings is recorded explicitly so that no consumer silently changes the convention. The twisted dual $M^\vee$ carries the left action $(r\cdot f)(m)=f(\psi(r)m)$; the double dual identifies with $M$ because $\psi^2=\mathrm{id}$ and finite-dimensional graded vector spaces are reflexive, with the grading bookkeeping $(M\{r\})^\#=M^\#\{-r\}$ from the internal shift convention. Indecomposability: $(-)^\#$ is exact (its underlying functor is $k$-duality, exact) and involutive, hence a contravariant equivalence on finite-dimensional graded modules; it exchanges projective and injective objects, which coincide over the graded Frobenius algebra $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]; therefore it preserves the classes of indecomposables and sends the shift orbit of $M$ to itself, i.e. $M^\#\cong M\{t(M)\}$ for a well-defined integer $t(M)$ on the shift orbit. The self-dual equation: $(M\{s\})^\#\cong M^\#\{-s\}\cong M\{t(M)-s\}$, so $M\{s\}^\#\cong M\{s\}$ iff $2s=t(M)$; the duality shift is even by the Frobenius form statement, so $s(M)=t(M)/2$ is the unique solution and the self-dual representative exists and is unique in each shift orbit. Compatibility with the generic $P_{i,n}$ normalization: the quotient map $R(|\beta|)\to R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is $\psi$-equivariant and carries the generic self-dual divided-power classes to cyclotomic self-dual classes up to the trace shift; the convention is declared here so that no consumer silently changes the shift. The definition is choice-free (the only choices are the fixed normalizations).

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction mixed relations and the rank-one exact sequence
items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Section 3.2, read in the library's block notation. The engine is the bimodule computation decomposing the corner $e(\beta,i)R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta)$ by the rank-one last strand: Corollary 3.8 exhibits the exact sequence of $(R(n),R(n))$-bimodules $0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk[t]\to0$ (the maps $\phi_1,\phi_2$ of (3.15)-(3.16) coincide after the identifications $R(n)\otimes_kI[x_{n+1}]=kI[x_1]\otimes R_1(n)=R(n)\otimes_kk[t]$, and left multiplication by $x_{n+1}$, right multiplication by $x_1$ both act as $t$). Part (b)'s isomorphism (Theorem 3.6) is a consequence of the corner decomposition $R(n)\otimes R(1)\hookrightarrow R(n+1)$ and the quadratic relation on the last two strands: the two possible orders of restriction and induction differ by the tensor factor $k[t_i]$ that records the surviving last-strand polynomial action, and the exponent $q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}$ is the degree $-b_{ii}=-2d_i$ of the relevant crossing. Part (a) for unequal colours is the same computation with $e(\beta,i)(R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_1)e(j,\beta)=0$ for $i\ne j$ (equation (3.15)), which gives the graded commutativity of the two inductions. Part (c) is Theorem 3.9(b), proved directly from Corollary 3.8 by applying the functor $-\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$: the kernel of $F_i$ is $\bar F_iE_i$, the cokernel is $M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ shifted by the degree $-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$ of the surviving coefficient, and the sequence is functorial in $M$. The degree conventions are those of the PBW theorem [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] and the divided-power projectives [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; no localization, trace or choice principle is used.

items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Section 4.3 (Theorems 4.5 and 4.7 and Corollary 4.6), with the explicit polynomial filtration of the design. (i) Reduction to the rank-one corner: by Lemma 4.3 applied to the last strand, there is a monic polynomial $g(u)\in k[u]$ with $g(x_n)=0$ in $R^\Lambda(\beta)$; the right $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is filtered by the $x_{n+1}$-powers $x_{n+1}^r e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ whose associated graded pieces are the kernels $K_0,K_1$ of the multiplication maps, and Lemmas 4.8-4.17 identify these as finitely generated projective right modules over $R^\Lambda(\beta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with the explicit maps $P:K_1\to K_0$ and $Q:R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)\to K_1$; Lemma 4.17 (an algebraic lemma on a projective module over $A\otimes k[t]$ with injective multiplication) makes the colon module projective. (ii) The same argument on the other side, using the anti-involution, gives the left-module statement, and Corollary 4.6 follows by tensoring a projective resolution. (iii) The exact sequence (4.10) is Theorem 4.7: it follows from the bimodule exact sequence of the generic mixed-relations lemma applied to the kernel of the quotient map $F_iM\to F^\Lambda_iM$, with the quotient by the cyclotomic ideal computed by Lemma 4.2; the shift exponent $(\alpha_i\mid2\Lambda-\beta)$ is KK's $(4.10)$ and comes from the degree of the cyclotomic relation plus the degree $-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$ of the generic last-strand coefficient. The stated projectivity uses only the polynomially filtered colon argument; no geometric or choice-theoretic input. The exponent is exactly KK's $q^{(\alpha_i\mid2\Lambda-\beta)}$; the divided-power normalization of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] fixes the meaning of the $q$-powers but no Gaussian quotient is divided here, so integrality of the shift is immediate.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator for cyclotomic KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\,\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$
(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\,\mathrm{Id}.$$
Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift conventions).
items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Theorem 5.2 with its proof in Section 5.2. For each $M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ build the commutative diagram (5.5) with exact rows and columns from three previously proved inputs: the generic mixed relations of [[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]] (Theorem 3.6 and Theorem 3.9 of the source), the cyclotomic comparison sequence of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-induction-is-projective-on-the-right]] (Theorem 4.7), and the exactness of $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$. The snake lemma produces maps $A,B,C$; the natural transformations $x_{E^\Lambda_i},x_{F^\Lambda_i}$ (left multiplication by $x_{n+1}$ on $E^\Lambda_i N$ and right multiplication by $x_{n+1}$ on the kernel of $F^\Lambda_i$) give the units and counits of the adjunction and the degree $-2$ pieces (5.3)-(5.4). The two sign cases are then separated: if $a:=\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$ the map $A$ is injective with the displayed cokernel $\bigoplus_{k=0}^{a-1}q_i^{2k}R^\Lambda(\beta)$; if $a\le0$ the cokernel of $A$ vanishes and $\Psi$ restricts to the triangular endomorphism $\Psi(t_i^j)=\gamma^{-1}t_i^{a-1-j}+\sum E(\psi_{j+k})t_i^k$ of $\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-a-1}kt_i^k\otimes R^\Lambda(\beta)$, which is an isomorphism because $\gamma\phi_k$ is monic of degree $k-a$ and hence the diagonal entries are units; this is the exact statement proved at the end of the source's Section 5.2. The $q$-powers are the fixed grading shifts ($q_i=q^{d_i}$, degrees of dots and crossings as in the presentation), and the summand count is the k-string length $|\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle|$ supplied by the cyclotomic vanishing $R^\Lambda(\beta+k\alpha_i)=0$; no AC is used.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.strategy: This is the standard Kashiwara--Miwa--Petersen--Yung Proposition B.1 step, proved locally. Fix $i$ and a vector $v$; by local nilpotence of $E_i,F_i$ on $v$, the span of $v$ under $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ is finite-dimensional and stable, and the mixed relations restricted to it are the rank-one relations integrated by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] (the divided-power commutation formula and the finite simple $U_{q_i}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules), giving an action of $U_{q_i}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ on that span with the prescribed torus characters. The quantum Serre relations among the $E_i$ and among the $F_i$ are then checked on these finite-dimensional local spans by the classical reduction: the operators $E_i,F_j$ for $i\ne j$ generate a locally finite rank-two span, and $(\mathrm{ad}\,F_i)^{1-a_{ij}}F_j=0$ follows from the explicit $A_2$ rank-two computation of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] applied to the highest-weight vectors appearing in each local span. Existence of the extension follows because every defining relation of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is verified on every vector, and uniqueness because $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by the torus and the $E_i,F_i$. Integrability is condition (b) together with the defining local-nilpotence requirement of [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]; finite-dimensional weight spaces then make the $i$-string decomposition theorem available verbatim. The argument is a finite computation on each local span; no choice principle is used and no highest-weight hypothesis is needed.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR functors give integrable quantum actions on $K_0$ and $G_0$
items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Section 6 down to Lemma 6.1, made explicit. (i) The exactness of $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ is [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-induction-is-projective-on-the-right]]; the shift factors in the definitions are exactly the $q_i^{1-\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$ normalizations of the source's two diagrams above Lemma 6.1, they make the operators weight-homogeneous, and $K_i$-linearity holds because $K_i$ acts by $q_i^{\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$ on the $\beta$-component. (ii) The mixed relation (a) is Lemma 6.1 and follows from the categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]]: on the class of $M$ in degree $\beta$, the commutator $E_iF_i-F_iE_i$ is the trace of the displayed finite summand decomposition, a geometric series in $q_i^2$ summing to $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; for $i\ne j$ the commutator vanishes by the same theorem's mixed case. (iii) Local nilpotence: $E_i$ lowers $\beta\mapsto\beta-\alpha_i$, so $E_i^k$ maps into the zero group once $\beta-k\alpha_i\notin Q_+$; $F_i$ raises it and $R^\Lambda(\beta+k\alpha_i)=0$ for $k\gg0$ by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]], so $F_i$ is even locally nilpotent componentwise. (iv) The integrable structures now follow from [[lem-mixed-relations-and-local-nilpotence-give-an-integrable-quantum-action]] with the label grading by $\beta\in Q_+$ and weight $\Lambda-\beta$; each Grothendieck class has finite support. (v) The pairing: $P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M$ is finite-dimensional in each degree and bounded below, so its gdim lies in $\mathbb Z((q))$; the central color-symmetric polynomial argument of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] applies to the finite-dimensional quotient and yields $A$-values. Nondegeneracy and adjointness are the source's statement that $E_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$, $F_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$ are adjoint to $F_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$, $E_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$, transported through HA-19's pairing theorems ([[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]). No AC is used.

items.title: The projective Grothendieck group is the integral highest weight module
items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Section 6, end of the section, together with the explicit map of Kleshchev's survey Proposition 9.3. Surjectivity: by [[lem-the-vacuum-projective-is-a-highest-weight-generator]] every class is an $A$-linear combination of $F^\Lambda$-words applied to $1_\Lambda$, so the map from $U_A$ induced by $F_i^{(n)}\mapsto F_i^{(n)}[1_\Lambda]$ is surjective; the divided powers agree with the ordinary powers up to the unit $[n]_{q_i}!$ by [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], so it suffices to use the divided-power generators. The ideal $\sum_iU_AF_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ lies in the kernel: $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}[1_\Lambda]$ is a class in $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda((\lambda_i+1)\alpha_i))]$, which is zero by the cyclotomic vanishing [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]] (KK's Lemma 4.3(b)). The resulting surjection $V_A(\Lambda)\twoheadrightarrow[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]$ is a map of integrable highest weight modules over $\mathbb Q(q)$; the target is generated by a highest weight vector of weight $\Lambda$ (the vacuum, killed by every $E_i$ by [[lem-the-vacuum-projective-is-a-highest-weight-generator]]) and is integrable by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]], so by the uniqueness of integrable highest weight modules ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]) the scalar extension is an isomorphism. Integrality: both sides are free $A$-modules (HA-19 shift-orbit bases for the left side; finite-rank weight spaces of the integral form on the right), and a surjection between free modules of equal rank over the domain $A$ is injective, so $\phi$ is an isomorphism. The Cartan/Shapovalov alternative for injectivity: the KLR Cartan pairing agrees with the Lusztig-normalized form $B_L$ on the negative half ([[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]]), the radical of $B_L$ is the annihilator of $v_\Lambda$ by the nondegeneracy ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]), and the nondegenerate descended form on $V_A(\Lambda)$ distinguishes classes, forcing injectivity of $\phi$; this clause is exactly where the Axiom of Choice is inherited. No other step uses it.

items.title: The module Grothendieck group is the dual integral highest weight module
items.statement:
Keep the field hypotheses of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]]; in particular the degree-zero part of the base ring is a field and every $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional over it. Write $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]$ for the Grothendieck group of graded $R^\Lambda$-modules finite-dimensional over $k$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]). Then:
(a) the assignments
$$\langle[P],[M]\rangle_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M\bigr)\qquad(P,M\in\text{finite graded modules, }P\text{ projective})$$
define an $A$-sesquilinear perfect pairing $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\times[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]\to A$, linear in the second variable and $q^{-1}$-linear in the first, with $\langle[P]\{r\},[M]\rangle=q^{-r}\langle[P],[M]\rangle$ and $\langle[P],[M]\{r\}\rangle=q^{r}\langle[P],[M]\rangle$, where the duality $(-)^\#$ is the one normalized in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] and $\psi$ the descended anti-involution of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]];
(b) the induced maps of $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]$ realize the dual operators: $E_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$ is adjoint to $F_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$ and $F_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$ to $E_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$ under this pairing, and the simple classes give the dual basis to the classes of the self-dual indecomposable projectives;
(c) consequently $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]$ is a free $A$-module and there is a canonical isomorphism
$$[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)^{\vee},$$
where $V_A(\Lambda)^{\vee}$ is the $A$-form of the contravariant-form dual of $V_A(\Lambda)$ normalized by [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] and [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]; the isomorphism sends the class of the rank-zero simple module to the dual highest-weight functional and intertwines the normalized operators of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] with the dual $U_A(\mathfrak g)$-action.
items.strategy: This is Kang--Kashiwara Section 6, the pairing paragraph, with the duality conventions fixed in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]. (i) Well-definedness and values: $P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M$ is finite-dimensional in each degree and bounded below, so its graded dimension is defined; the finite-dimensional quotient algebra has finitely generated graded pieces and the gdim of the tensor is a finite Laurent polynomial; sums over the finitely many projective summands preserve this. (ii) Perfectness: over a finite-dimensional graded Frobenius algebra, $\mathrm{HOM}_k(P,k)$ with the $\psi$-twist is again a (shifted) projective, and the tensor-Hom evaluation $\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda}(P,R^\Lambda)\otimes_{R^\Lambda}M\to\mathrm{HOM}_{R^\Lambda}(P,M)$ is an isomorphism for finite projective $P$ (the generic computation of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]], now finite-dimensional, so the argument is shorter: both sides are additive in $P$ and are checked on principal projectives, where both identify with the corresponding idempotent corner of $M$). This gives the pairing as the composition of the Hom pairing with the $\#$-duality, hence perfectness and the stated $\#$-, shift- and variance-properties, and it shows that the simple-class basis is dual to the self-dual-projective-class basis (HA-19's dual-basis statement [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] transported along the normalization). (iii) Adjointness: the exact functors $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ induce the exact-sequence operators, and the adjointness in the pairing is the source's statement that $E_i|[\mathrm{Proj}],F_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$ are adjoint to $F_i|[\mathrm{Rep}],E_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$; the normalized shifts of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] are the ones making the adjointness degree-zero. (iv) The identification with $V_A(\Lambda)^\vee$: since $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] and the pairing is perfect, restriction of functionals identifies $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]$ with the $A$-module of $A$-linear functionals on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]$; transporting the dual $U_A(\mathfrak g)$-action along the adjunction and the contravariant form of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] gives the stated isomorphism, normalized by [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]. Both sides are free $A$-modules, so no additional divisibility is asserted. No AC is used.

items.title: Simple and projective crystals of the cyclotomic quotient are $B(\Lambda)$
items.strategy: This is Lauda--Vazirani's crystal theorem for cyclotomic quotients (Theorems 7.4 and 7.5), read in the library's conventions. (i) The socle/head operators: Lauda--Vazirani Section 2.5 proves that for a self-dual simple $M$ the restriction $E^\Lambda_iM$ has socle a direct sum of $[m]_{q_i}!$ copies of a single self-dual simple, for $m=\varepsilon_i(M)$; this uses the rank-one theory of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] and the idempotent recursion, and is the definition of $\tilde e_i$. Existence of $\tilde f_i$ is the corresponding head statement, obtained from the same recursion with the two restrictions $E^\Lambda_i$ and the left-append restriction; the integer identities $\varepsilon_i(\tilde f_i[M])=\varepsilon_i(M)+1$ and $\varphi_i(\tilde f_i[M])=\varphi_i(M)-1$ are (6.119)-(6.120) in the source. (ii) The crystal axioms are checked in Lauda--Vazirani Section 5.3 and Theorem 7.5: axiom (M2) (weights), (M3),(M4) (strictness of the embeddings) are exactly Propositions 7.1-7.3, built from the strict embedding $\Psi_i:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B\otimes B_i$ of the negative-half crystal; the connectedness and highest weight property come from $\varepsilon_i^\vee$-reduction. (iii) Identification with $B(\Lambda)$: the source's Theorem 7.4 identifies the negative-half crystal $\mathcal B\cong B(\infty)$ and Theorem 7.5 identifies $\mathcal B_\Lambda\cong B(\Lambda)$ via Kashiwara's embedding $B(\Lambda)\hookrightarrow B(\infty)\otimes T_\Lambda$; in the library the target $B(\Lambda)$ is the canonical highest weight crystal of [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]], and the identification is an application of the uniqueness of highest weight crystals [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]: a connected crystal generated by a highest weight element of weight $\Lambda$ with the correct rank-one string data is $B(\Lambda)$. (iv) Projective side: by the perfect pairing of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] the simple class basis is dual to the self-dual projective class basis, and the adjointness of $E_i|[\mathrm{Proj}]$ and $F_i|[\mathrm{Rep}]$ converts the simple-crystal operators into the projective-crystal operators; the identification with the integral highest weight module is [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]]. The uniqueness clause inherits the Axiom of Choice through [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]; the socle/head indexing, the pairing duality and the rank-one string computations are choice-free.

items.title: Cyclotomic extension of scalars respects the based quotient (conditional)
items.statement:
Keep the first-strand/right-append conventions of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] and the word mirror $\rho$ of [[lem-word-mirror-involution-of-a-klr-algebra-and-the-quantum-star]], and let $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ be the negative-half categorification of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Assume the generic lower-global-basis theorem [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-klr-projectives-give-the-negative-half-lower-global-basis]] is supplied. Then:
(a) **Side convention.** The extension-of-scalars functor $R^\Lambda\otimes_R(-)$ on finite graded projectives induces on $K_0$ the map $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$, where $\pi_\Lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\Lambda)$ is the canonical surjection of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] and $*$ is the anti-automorphism of the negative half with $F_i^*=F_i$ and $q^*=q$ exhibited by the word mirror; composing the functor with the twisting equivalence of $\rho$ replaces $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$ by $\pi_\Lambda$. With the last-strand form of the cyclotomic relation and left-append induction the star is absent and the same statements hold verbatim for $\pi_\Lambda$.
(b) **Zero/survival.** For every lower global basis vector $G^-(\theta)$ of $V_A(\Lambda)$ with $\theta\in A f$ ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) the class $R^\Lambda\otimes_R\gamma(\theta)$ equals $\gamma^\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda(\theta))$, which is a single normalized lower-global-basis projective class $[P^\Lambda_\theta]$ when $\pi_\Lambda(\theta)\ne0$ and $0$ otherwise ([[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]).
(c) **Indecomposable-or-zero.** For the normalized self-dual indecomposable generic projective $P_\theta$ representing $\gamma(\theta)$, the extension-of-scalars module $R^\Lambda\otimes_RP_\theta$ is again a single normalized indecomposable projective, or zero. The proof uses the HA-19 shift-orbit bases of $K_0$ and the nonnegativity of Krull--Schmidt multiplicities ([[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]) together with the finite-dimensional graded quotient argument: a $\psi$-stable homogeneous quotient of a finite graded projective is zero or indecomposable-projective, projective duality commutes with the quotient, and the surviving projective-cover shift orbits do not merge.
items.strategy: The algebraic content is the owner's future-cyclotomic quotient proof, combined with the based-quotient projection theorem. (i) Writing $B=R^\Lambda\otimes_RA$ for a finite graded projective $A$-module $P$ over the generic algebra: $B$ is finite graded projective because $P$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifts of $R$, and extension of scalars sends shifted free modules to shifted free modules. When $A\to B$ is a quotient by a homogeneous two-sided ideal $J$, the degree-zero endomorphism algebra of $P_B$ is $\mathrm{End}_A^0(P)/$ (maps factoring through $J$), which is a quotient of the local finite-dimensional algebra $\mathrm{End}_A^0(P)$, hence local; a local algebra has no nontrivial idempotents, so $P_B$ is zero or indecomposable. If moreover $P\to S$ is a projective cover with $JS=0$, then $P_B\to S$ is again a projective cover (a preimage argument using essentiality), and if $JS\ne0$ and $P_B$ has a simple quotient then $P_B=0$ because every simple quotient factors through the unique simple head $S$. Finite projective duality commutes with the quotient: $\mathrm{HOM}_B(P_B,B)^\psi\cong B\otimes_A\mathrm{HOM}_A(P,A)^\psi$, because the finite-projective Hom base change is an isomorphism and the $\psi$-twist interchanges the left and right actions while $\psi(J)=J$; hence self-duality of $P$ survives on every nonzero quotient. (ii) Side convention: the Grothendieck class of the word projective $P_{i_1,\dots,i_n}=R(n)e(i_1,\dots,i_n)$ is the ordered product of the $F$-classes, while the first-strand cyclotomic relation kills the *first* letter; comparing with the highest weight quotient generated by the vacuum and killed by the $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$-left-ideal gives the multiplication-reversing star, as computed in the word-mirror lemma; the mirror twist removes the star. This is exactly why the lemma records the two equivalent formulations. (iii) Zero/survival: QG-5's projection theorem says that the image of a lower global basis vector under $\pi_\Lambda$ is zero or another lower global basis vector; applying it to the $K_0$-isomorphism of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] and using additivity of extension of scalars on the triangular basis gives (b). (iv) Combining (i) and (iii): the extension-of-scalars object has a class which is a single normalized basis class or zero, and by (i) the object is indecomposable-projective or zero; its normalization is the one fixed in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]. *Conditional clause and present blocker:* every step after the side convention consumes [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-klr-projectives-give-the-negative-half-lower-global-basis]], which is an owner-escalated subject of batch 10 (the geometric realization stack of Varagnolo--Vasserot Theorem 4.5 is not available in-run); the lemma is therefore scaffolded as conditional and is not recorded ready. The Axiom of Choice is used only through the QG-5 based-quotient suppliers, which reach it via the negative-half form; the quotient/duality argument itself is choice-free.

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic KLR projectives give the lower global basis
items.statement: In symmetric Cartan type over a field of characteristic zero, with the same quiver-geometric parameter regime and the same loopless quiver with arbitrary edge multiplicities $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the generic basis theorem [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-klr-projectives-give-the-negative-half-lower-global-basis]], the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] maps the normalized classes of the self-dual indecomposable projective $R^\Lambda$-modules bijectively onto the lower global basis of $V_A(\Lambda)$ ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]): for every lower global vector $G^-(\theta)$ there is a unique normalized self-dual indecomposable projective $P^\Lambda_\theta$ with $[P^\Lambda_\theta]\mapsto G^-(\theta)$, and this assignment is inverse to taking extension of scalars from the generic normalized self-dual projectives of the generic theorem. The normalization is the self-dual shift of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] and the form comparison is the Lusztig-normalized one of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]] ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the $q_i$-powers); no arbitrary-parameter extension is asserted, and any extension to arbitrary KLR parameters requires its own proved invariance theorem.
items.strategy: Combine the conditional based-quotient lemma with the projection theorem and the generic theorem. (i) By [[lem-cyclotomic-extension-of-scalars-respects-the-based-quotient]] (whose hypotheses explicitly include the generic theorem), extension of scalars sends each normalized generic self-dual indecomposable projective class $\gamma(\theta)$ (the image of a lower global vector, by the generic theorem) to a single normalized cyclotomic self-dual indecomposable projective class or zero, according to whether $\pi_\Lambda(\theta)$ survives. (ii) QG-5's projection theorem [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]] identifies the survival pattern with the lower global basis of $V_A(\Lambda)$: the surviving classes are exactly $\{G^-(\pi_\Lambda(\theta))\ne0\}$, and the map $\theta\mapsto\pi_\Lambda(\theta)$ is the triangular projection onto $V_A(\Lambda)$. (iii) The resulting family is unitriangular with respect to the bar-invariant basis and consists of bar-invariant normalized classes, so it equals the lower global basis: injectivity and surjectivity follow because both are bases of the same free $A$-module and the triangular matrix has unit diagonal. (iv) The form normalization enters in fixing the signs and the scalars: the KLR Cartan pairing agrees with the Lusztig-normalized form $B_L$ by [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]] and the divided-power normalization [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], so the cyclotomic projective classes and the lower global vectors have the same norm data. *Conditional clause and present blocker:* the argument consumes [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-klr-projectives-give-the-negative-half-lower-global-basis]] (owner-escalated in batch 10 because the semisimple quiver-flag Ext realization is not available in-run) and is therefore scaffolded as conditional; it is not recorded ready, and no independent VV-style formality is assumed. Axiom of Choice is inherited from the same suppliers.

items.title: Self-dual simple cyclotomic KLR modules give the upper global basis
items.statement: In the same symmetric-Cartan, characteristic-zero, quiver-geometric regime as [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]], the dual isomorphism $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)^\vee$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] maps the normalized classes of the self-dual simple $R^\Lambda$-modules bijectively onto the upper global basis of $V_A(\Lambda)$ ([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]), dual to the lower global basis of the projective theorem under the contravariant pairing; the correspondence is inverse to the $\#$-duality between self-dual simples and self-dual indecomposable projectives fixed by the self-dual shift normalization, and the grading normalization is the unique one of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]. The crystal compatibility of the two families is the identification of [[thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda]] with $B(\Lambda)$; the duality of the two bases is [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]. No extension beyond the stated parameter regime is asserted.
items.strategy: Deduce from the projective identification and the perfect pairing. (i) By [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] and the lower-basis theorem [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]], the self-dual indecomposable projective classes are the lower global basis under the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$. (ii) The perfect pairing of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] makes $[\mathrm{Rep}]$ the dual $A$-module and the simple classes the dual basis to the projective classes; under the contravariant form this dual basis is exactly the upper global basis by definition [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], and QG-5's theorem [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] records that the two families are the upper and lower global bases and are crystal compatible. (iii) The normalization: for a self-dual simple $S$ the pairing identifies its class with the functional dual to its $\#$-dual projective, and the equality of the two normalizations is the compatibility of the self-dual shift with the trace pairing (the trace is invariant under $\psi$ and cyclicity of the Frobenius form). (iv) Crystal compatibility is [[thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda]]. *Conditional clause and present blocker:* the theorem consumes [[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]] and hence the owner-escalated generic geometric global-basis theorem; it is scaffolded as conditional and not recorded ready. Axiom of Choice is inherited through the QG-5 duality theorem and the generic basis suppliers.

title: Cyclotomic KLR Algebras and Highest-Weight Categorification — Examples

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
items.statement:
Work over a field $k$ with a symmetrizable Cartan datum with no imaginary simple roots and a dominant integral weight $\Lambda$, using the standard cyclotomic polynomials $a^\Lambda_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$, $\lambda_i=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle$.
(a) Rank $0$: $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ by definition, with one simple module and $[1_\Lambda]=[k]$.
(b) Rank $1$: for every $i\in I$ there is a graded algebra isomorphism $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k[x_1]/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$, with $k$-basis $1,x_1,\dots,x_1^{\lambda_i-1}$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$; its Frobenius trace is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_i-1}$ and has degree $2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. In particular $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=0$ when $\lambda_i=0$ and $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k$ when $\lambda_i=1$; the unique simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, and $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ is its projective cover.
(c) Rank-one higher weights: in the rank-one case $I=\{i\}$, the algebra $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)$ is the quotient of the nil-Hecke algebra $NH_n$ by $x_1^{\lambda_i}=0$; it is nonzero for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$ and zero for $n>\lambda_i$, and the number of isomorphism classes of self-dual simple $R^\Lambda$-modules is $\lambda_i+1$, matching the dimension of $V(\lambda_i\Lambda_i)$. For $\lambda_i=1$ the vanishing is elementary: the relation $x_1e(\nu)=0$ propagates through the mixed relations to $x_2e(\nu)=0$ and then to $\tau e(\nu)=0$, so that already $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=0$.
items.strategy:
(a) and (b) are immediate from the definition of the cyclotomic quotient and the PBW basis [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]: at rank $1$ there are no crossings, $x_1$ is central, and the relations are $x_1^{\lambda_i}=0$ with no other relation, so the quotient is the truncated polynomial ring; the PBW monomials $x_1^r$, $0\le r<\lambda_i$, form a basis and the graded dimension and the trace degree $2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$ follow from $\deg x_1=2d_i$ and [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]. (c) $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$ is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke algebra; that it vanishes for $n>\lambda_i$ is Kang--Kashiwara Lemma 4.3(b) in the rank-one case (the propagation of monic annihilating polynomials along equal colours uses Lemma 4.2), and it can be checked directly for $\lambda_i=1$: from $x_1e(
u)=0$ and the mixed relation $x_1	au=	au x_2-e$ (in the sign-normalization of the presentation) one gets $x_2	au e(

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_i k=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i k=0$.
(b) The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$, $\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus \mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i k\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$.
(c) Consequently, with the normalized operators of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]], on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so $[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with $K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back, $F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] verified at the first nontrivial weight.
items.strategy: (a) is the rank-one part of the previous example, together with the vanishing $R^\Lambda(3\alpha_i)=0$ forced by the propagation argument for $\lambda_i=2$ (Kang--Kashiwara Lemma 4.3(b)): $x_1^2=0$ propagates to a monic relation of degree $3$ on $x_2$, and the rank-two quotient is already zero at length three. $E^\Lambda_i(R^\Lambda(\alpha_i))=e(0,i)R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ as a weight-zero vector space, of graded dimension $1+q^2$, and $E^\Lambda_i k=0$ because $e(-,i)$ has no support at weight $0$. (b) The theorem's isomorphism at $\beta=0$: since $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ applied to the vacuum is $F^\Lambda_i(0)=0$, the right side $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i(k)=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k\oplus k\{2\}$ equals the identity summands $\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}$ — the empty $k$-sum and the two required summands; the shift $q^{-2}$ on the vanishing term is invisible. (c) Normalized operators: on $[\mathrm{Proj}(\alpha_i)]$ the operator $E_i$ carries the factor $q^{1-\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$ with target weight $\beta=0$, i.e. $q^{1-2}=q^{-1}$; hence $E_i[R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)]=q^{-1}(1+q^2)[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$, while $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=F_i(0)=0$. On $[\mathrm{Rep}]$: $F_i[k]=q^{1-2}F^\Lambda_i[k]=q^{-1}([k]\oplus q^2[k])=(q^{-1}+q)[k]$ in weight $\alpha_i$, and $E_i$ (unshifted here) sends it back to $(q^{-1}+q)[k]$, while $F_iE_i[k]=F_i(0)=0$; the right-hand side $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ with $K_i[k]=q^{\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle}=q^2$ evaluates to $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})=q+q^{-1}$. All shifts are the fixed grading shifts of the source's Section 6 and the divided-power conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]; the check also shows the two different normalization locations (target weight for $E_i$ on $[\mathrm{Proj}]$, source weight for $F_i$ on $[\mathrm{Rep}]$) are exactly what makes the identity degree-homogeneous. No AC is used.

items.title: Self-dual shift normalization for a cyclotomic projective
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$, $d_i=1$, and $\Lambda=\lambda\Lambda_1$; then $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/(x^\lambda)$, and let $P:=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ be the indecomposable projective of weight $\alpha_i$. Then:
(a) $(R^\Lambda(\alpha_i))^\#\cong R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\{2(\lambda-1)\}$: the graded dual is again the regular module shifted by twice the socle degree.
(b) The self-dual representative of the shift orbit of $P$ is $P_{i,1}^\natural:=P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$, the unique shift $s$ with $(P\{s\})^\#\cong P\{s\}$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)=t/2$ for $t=2(\lambda-1)$; this is the cyclotomic instance of the normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]].
(c) For $\lambda=1$ the shift vanishes and $P$ is self-dual as it stands; for $\lambda=2$, $P=k[x]/(x^2)$ has $P\{-1\}$ as its self-dual representative, and $(P\{-1\})^\#\cong P\{-1\}$ holds because $t=2$ is even. The same halving rule applies to the rank-one divided-power projectives of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] under the quotient.
items.strategy: Everything is the rank-one computation of the Frobenius form. (a) On $k[x]/(x^\lambda)$ with $\deg x=2$, the pairing $(a,b)\mapsto$ coefficient of $x^{\lambda-1}$ in $ab$ is perfect, symmetric and homogeneous of degree $2(\lambda-1)$: the monomial basis is triangular with diagonal entries $1$. The induced algebra isomorphism $R\cong R^\vee\{t\}$ with $t=2(\lambda-1)$ gives (a) by tensoring the bimodule isomorphism with the identity, or directly via the trace pairing on the principal projective: $\mathrm{HOM}_k(R,k)^\psi\cong R\{t\}$. (b) The equation $(M\{s\})^\#=M^\#\{-s\}\cong M\{t-s\}$ has the unique solution $s=t/2$ when $t$ is even, and $t=2(\lambda-1)$ is even; this is the definition of the self-dual normalization. (c) The cases $\lambda=1,2$ are the explicit substitutions. The trace cyclicity of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]] is what makes the twisted dual a left-module isomorphism rather than merely a linear one. No AC is used.

items.title: K_0 categorification alone does not identify the global basis
items.statement:
**Statement refuted:** once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are automatically lower global basis vectors; in particular the K_0-level categorification alone identifies the global basis.
**Counterexample (rank two, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$).** Let $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the word projective is $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$, which is not indecomposable: by the rank-one case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] it is a direct sum of $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective $P_{i,2}$, so its class is
$$[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})\,[P_{i,2}].$$
Under $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(2\Lambda_1)$ the class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ is the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, while the lower global basis vector in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the divided power $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}=F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}/[2]_{q_i}$; the two differ by the scalar $q+q^{-1}\notin\{\pm q^n\}$, so no K_0-level statement that only names the module $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)$ and its class can decide between them. The lower global basis is picked out only by the additional structure: the self-dual shift normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], bar invariance, and the positivity of the divided-power coefficients, none of which is part of the bare $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ statement. The example also shows the true positive claim: the lower global class in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the class of the *indecomposable* projective $P_{i,2}$, not of the word projective.
items.strategy: Compute the two classes in the rank-one quotient and compare. (i) $NH_2$ has the PBW basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$ and $NH_2\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ given by the polynomial-column decomposition (KL I Section 2.2 and Section 3.1, quoted in [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]); the cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$ is a finite-dimensional graded quotient in which the same projective cover decomposition persists with the shift centering $P_{i,2}$ (the projective decomposition is the rank-two case of the divided-power construction, with the cyclotomic quotient acting on the finitely many PBW classes), hence the displayed class identity. (ii) In $U^-_A(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ one has $F_i^2=[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}$ by the definition of the divided power, so under the K_0 isomorphism the word class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ corresponds to $[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$; the lower global basis vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] specialized to the rank-one module. (iii) The scalar $[2]_{q_i}=q+q^{-1}$ is not of the form $\pm q^n$; a rescaling of a basis vector by a non-unit is not a basis change over $A$, so the word class cannot be the global basis element in that weight, and no purely $K_0$-theoretic identification can produce the divided power without dividing by $[2]_{q_i}$. This refutes the stated claim and simultaneously records where the missing input lives: the self-dual normalization and positivity of the extension-of-scalars theorem. No AC is used.
